To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the length of alkylene-based side spacers plays an important role in the self-structuring of alkylene-based diurea cross-linkers, while the inclusion of long side spacers does not affect the structure of the hybrids.

the length of side spacers plays an important role in the structuration of lamellar bridging silsesquioxane hybrids, and that the emission of the urea cross-linked alkyl-bridged hybrids depends on the side spacers length.

the length of alkylene-based side spacers in diurea cross-linkages has a unique effect on the structuring of the alkylene chains in the lamellar structure of the materials and that the emission features depend critically on the conformation of the side spacer chains.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of a new family of alkylene-based hybrids, the C(10)(C(n)C)(10) BSs, that are characterized by the presence of decylene chains as spacers.

the synthesis of new alkylene-based BS materials with decylene chains as spacers, the self-assembly of which has been investigated through a combination of X-ray diffraction, solid-state NMR, and photophysical techniques.
the synthesis, structural characterization, and photophysical properties of a series of diurea crosslinked BSs incorporating long side spacers and central spacers with variable length.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the length of side spacers plays an important role in determining the degree of ordering of alkylene-based bridged silsesiquoxanes, while their morphology remains unaffected by the presence of decylene instead propylene side chains.
the length of side spacers in alkylene-based bridged silsesqioxane hybrids is a key factor that controls the structuring of the alkylene-based BS materials, while their morphology remains unaffected.

the length of side spacers plays the major role in determining the emission features of urea cross-linked alkoxysilane-based BSs, while the length of the central spacer is responsible for the structural organization of the hybrids.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
alkylene-based BS hybrids are more sensitive than oxyethylene-based ones to the length of the alkyl chains, which can be used as a tool to control the emission properties of these materials.

the emission features and quantum yields of the urea-based component in alkylene-based BS hybrids are determined by the length of the alkylene chains and the degree of structuring of the urea cross-linked arrays.
the emission of alkylurea cross-linked BSs is not exclusively related to the length of the alkylene central spacer but also to that of the side spacer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the length of side spacers plays an important role in the self-structuring of BSs, although this parameter has a limited influence on their photoluminescent properties.
the inclusion of decylene chains in the alkylene-based BS family leads to the formation and structuring of the urea cross-linked arrays, which is the key feature of the diureasils.
the side spacers of alkylene-based diurea BSs can be used to control the emission properties of the materials.
